correctness.rationale: The four cell sums omit only the two marked activities; their determinant gives Cov=-x_e x_f(Z10 Z01-Z00 Z11)/Z² with the original normalization. The independent replay in branches/15333b53-a4cb-4a50-91da-58ef995f75f5/independent_check.py exhausted 1024 subsets and recomputed all 45 unordered pairs, not just sample activities. It verified all quotients by multiplication by q²(1-q), independently generated the eight S2×S3 pair orbits of sizes 6,3,6,3,6,12,6,3, and matched every table. Their term counts are 32,28,82,82,76,82,68,78. Seven quotients are nonzero and coefficientwise nonnegative. Pair (1,5), i.e. {0,2} and {1,3}, has exactly the coefficients -50 of q^0 v^5 w and -20 of q^0 v^6 w as its negative terms. All positive-q-degree coefficients are nonnegative. In degree zero subtracting 25v^4(v-w)^2+v^5(84v²-20vw+96w²) leaves 14 strictly positive terms; the quadratic has positive leading coefficient and discriminant -31856. Hence that quotient is strictly positive too. The sign follows for all 0<q<1, v,w>0 and gives zero at q=1 by the factor, as expected. This does not cover fully heterogeneous ordinary activities or negative association. See replay-notes.md in the replay directory for the exact remainder and replay output. The frozen verifier was inspected, not executed.

evidence: Theorem 1.9 gives nonpositive covariance for common activity at least 1; Proposition 5.7 gives a pair-specific weighted sufficient condition and yields coverage for all activities at least 2. The high-degree paper's growing-degree regular sequences at homogeneous p do not give the finite mixed-weight K5 conclusion.

Theorem 1.1 of arXiv:2611.11993 gives a general upper bound on R=P(X_e=X_f=1)/(P(X_e=1)P(X_f=1)) that can be above 1. Theorem 1.3, §1 equations (1.9)–(1.14), sharpens it using the deleted-graph probability ν(J), implying nonpositive covariance if ν(J)≥(1-q)/(4q). For q<1/5 this threshold exceeds 1, so that sign implication cannot cover the full asserted interval.
broader_coverage.reasoning: There is broader graph/weight scope in ratio bounds, but not the same strict sign conclusion. The complete-graph sign result directly overlaps, but its activity hypotheses reach only part of the domain.

value.rationale: K5 is a natural finite complete graph outside the small-rank and small-corank theorem. It probes whether known lower activity bounds reflect essential behavior on this host. The one independent defect tests robustness under unrestricted single-bond inhomogeneity, and all-pair certification reaches the low-activity region where the general sufficient conditions do not apply. The single mixed-sign quotient explains why naive coefficientwise positivity is insufficient, while its exact decomposition proves the sign uniformly; this gives a usable benchmark beyond positive-activity sampling or the already-covered high-activity regimes.
